Fluid region is just the bore: a Ø60 mm × 42 mm cylinder (bolt holes are dry, outside the bore, so they don't touch the water). I'll split its lateral surface at z=20 and z=22 mm to get flange-bore-1 / gasket / flange-bore-2, plus inlet and outlet discs. Everything in metres. First cell: build the three stacked segments and measure.

```python
import os, subprocess
from build123d import *

R      = 0.030   # bore radius, m (60 mm dia)
T_FL   = 0.020   # flange thickness
T_GK   = 0.002   # gasket thickness
L      = 2*T_FL + T_GK

seg1 = Pos(0, 0, T_FL/2)              * Cylinder(R, T_FL)
seg2 = Pos(0, 0, T_FL + T_GK/2)       * Cylinder(R, T_GK)
seg3 = Pos(0, 0, T_FL + T_GK + T_FL/2)* Cylinder(R, T_FL)
fluid = seg1 + seg2 + seg3

bb = fluid.bounding_box()
print("bbox", bb.min, bb.max)
print("length z =", bb.max.Z - bb.min.Z, "want", L)
print("diameter =", bb.max.X - bb.min.X, "want", 2*R)
print("volume   =", fluid.volume, "want", 3.141592653589793*R*R*L)
os.makedirs("constant/triSurface", exist_ok=True)
```
Shape is right. Now one refinement step (2 mm background cells) and a clearance check on the bolt circle.

**Built and meshed.** The water volume is the bore only: a Ø60 mm × 42 mm cylinder, split axially into flange-20 mm / gasket-2 mm / flange-20 mm so each wetted band is its own patch. Bolt holes are dry and, at 140 mm PCD with Ø14 mm holes, their inner edge sits at r = 63 mm — far outside the 30 mm bore — so they cut nothing from the fluid; I did not model them.

Measured against the request (all in metres):
- bore diameter 0.0600 (want 0.060); face-to-face length 0.0420 (want 0.042 = 20+2+20)
- mesh volume 1.18668e-4 vs exact πR²L = 1.18752e-4 (−0.07 %)
- inlet / outlet areas 0.002827 each = πR² exactly; z = 0.0000 and 0.0420
- flangeBore1 z ∈ [0.0000, 0.0200], gasketInner z ∈ [0.0200, 0.0220] (2.0 mm band), flangeBore2 z ∈ [0.0220, 0.0420]; wall areas 0.003770 / 0.000377 / 0.003770 = exact 2πR·t; all wall points at r = 0.0300

Five STLs (`inlet, outlet, flangeBore1, gasketInner, flangeBore2`) were written to `constant/triSurface` from the named faces before meshing — patch names come from the surfaces themselves, never from bounding-box position — with feature edges extracted and snapped, so the three seam circles are crisp. snappyHexMesh on a 2 mm background box: 23 245 cells, max non-orthogonality 47.1, max skewness 1.21, `Mesh OK`.

Not checked: no boundary layers were added (`addLayers false`), so near-wall spacing is just the cut-cell size; and the flange/gasket solids themselves are not meshed — only the fluid, as asked.
